manuscript_summary.research_question: Does intervention X improve outcome Y?
manuscript_summary.approach: Single observational cohort with pre/post outcome measurement.
manuscript_summary.main_results: Mean outcome Y increases from 50 to 60 units after treatment in 80 participants.
manuscript_summary.claimed_contribution: Intervention X causes a 20% improvement in outcome Y.
manuscript_summary.developmental_stage: Demonstration manuscript with a central causal claim.

claims.text: Intervention X causes a 20% improvement in outcome Y.
alternatives: A 20% pre/post association is observed in the cohort.

evidence_anchors.quote_or_fact: A single observational cohort of 80 participants received intervention X. There was no randomized control group.

candidate_concerns.title: The design does not identify the headline causal effect
candidate_concerns.failure_mechanism: A single-group pre-post comparison has no concurrent counterfactual and cannot separate intervention effects from time trends, regression to the mean, co-interventions, or other changes.
candidate_concerns.scientific_consequence: The evidence can support a within-cohort pre-post association but cannot identify the stated causal treatment effect.
candidate_concerns.minimum_resolution: Reframe the central conclusion as associational unless a design or analysis that credibly identifies the treatment effect is available.
candidate_concerns.closure_criterion: The title, abstract, and conclusion no longer make a causal claim, or the manuscript provides and validates a defensible identification strategy with appropriate comparison data.
suggested_validation_checks: Check whether any concurrent comparison group or identification strategy is described elsewhere in the manuscript.

strengths: The pre/post numerical result is stated clearly.

specialist_requests.objective: Audit whether the design identifies the central causal claim.

notes: The core concern already captures the decisive causal-identification limitation.

core_verify:MC-CORE-REVIEWER-0001.steelman: The authors may intend the word 'causes' as informal shorthand for the observed pre/post change.
core_verify:MC-CORE-REVIEWER-0001.steelman_survival_reason: The abstract and conclusion explicitly state a causal effect, so the distinction between association and causation remains scientifically consequential.
core_verify:MC-CORE-REVIEWER-0001.rationale: The manuscript anchor directly establishes a single uncontrolled pre/post design, while the central claim is explicitly causal. The requested resolution is limited to correcting that mismatch or supplying a defensible identification strategy.
